expect_from_test: redact of the xml literal. The literal is three adjacent strings joined with \ continuations, which drop the newline and the indent, so the input is one line and there is no space between </username> and <password>. The test does not assert_eq the whole string. It asserts !contains the hex 2be98afc86aa7b88bb81cbe788fc0fce5, !contains plain-secret, contains <username>sa</username>, contains <httpPassword>[REDACTED:xml-password-element]</httpPassword>, and roxmltree_like_balanced (the count of < equals the count of >; both are 11 here, and the test does not assert 11). kettle-encrypted-password matches first and replaces the Encrypted hex. xml-password-element then matches <password> because its value group is [^<]+ and the kettle placeholder contains no <, so that element is xml-password-element too. The test never names the kettle label on this call. <password/> has no text and stays. <name>dwh</name> is not asserted.

redact of the kettle.properties line, including its trailing newline. The test asserts only !contains the hex. It does not assert the kettle label or the newline. The output keeps both: generic-assigned-secret does not take the placeholder, because [ is outside that pattern's value class. expect is the whole string redact returns.

assert_eq!(redact(plain, &cfg()), plain). Encrypted at rest is not eight hex digits, so kettle-encrypted-password does not match. <passes> is not password or passwd, so xml-password-element does not match. The string is unchanged.

The test does not assert_eq the whole string. It asserts contains [REDACTED:aws-access-key-id], !contains AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP, contains "key = ", and contains " end". Those four hold of this output. The pattern AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16} replaces the whole key and nothing around it.

The test builds the token as format!("ghp_{}", "a".repeat(36)) and redacts format!("token: {token}"). It asserts contains [REDACTED:github-token] and !contains the token. It does not assert_eq the whole string. The input here is that format expanded: ghp_ and then 36 a's. The pattern gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,} replaces only the token, so the output is token: [REDACTED:github-token].

The test does not assert_eq the whole string. It asserts contains [REDACTED:private-key-block], !contains MIIBOgIBAAJBAK, contains before, and contains after. The pem literal is BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY, a newline, MIIBOgIBAAJBAK, a newline, END RSA PRIVATE KEY, wrapped as before\n{pem}\nafter. The private-key-block pattern replaces the whole block, newlines included, and leaves the before and after lines.

The test does not assert_eq. It asserts contains [REDACTED:jwt] and !contains the jwt. The input is exactly one jwt match (eyJ, a dot, eyJ, a dot, the signature), so the whole string is the placeholder.

The test does not assert_eq the whole string. It asserts contains [REDACTED:generic-assigned-secret] and !contains hunter2fake. It does not assert that the field name or the quotes survive; the next test does, on a different literal. expect is the whole string: the value group is hunter2fake, and the field name, the equals sign, and both quotes stay.
assert_eq! the whole string to api_key: "[REDACTED:generic-assigned-secret]".to_string(), — the field name, the colon, both quotes, and .to_string(), stay, and only consumer-key is replaced.

assert_eq! the whole string to api_secret: "[REDACTED:generic-assigned-secret]".to_string(),. The label alternation matches the whole identifier api_secret, not the substring secret, so the api_ prefix is not left glued to the placeholder.

assert_eq! the whole string to access_token_secret: "[REDACTED:generic-assigned-secret]".to_string(),. Same word-boundary case, second call in the test: the match is the whole identifier access_token_secret.

assert_eq!(out, line) where line is api_key=settings.azure_openai_api_key,. The value is a dotted chain of identifiers, skip_dotted_identifier_refs is set on generic-assigned-secret, and the line is returned unchanged. The failure message is "a dotted identifier reference must be left untouched".

The test asserts only contains [REDACTED:generic-assigned-secret]. It does not assert that api_key= survives or that the whole value was the match. The value 1.2.3.4-not-an-identifier contains dots but a segment starts with a digit, so it is not a code reference and the value is replaced. expect is the whole string redact returns.
assert_eq!(redact(text, &cfg()), text) for fn main() { println!("hello world"); }. No built-in pattern matches.

RedactionConfig { extra_patterns: vec![("internal-token", r"ITKN-[0-9a-f]{8}")], extra_excluded_globs: Vec::new() }. The test asserts only contains [REDACTED:internal-token]. Extra patterns replace the whole match and have no value group. token= is not a built-in label, so it stays. expect is the whole string.

Same config as #extra, second call. The test asserts only contains [REDACTED:aws-access-key-id], the comment being that the baseline still fires alongside the extra pattern. It does not assert_eq the whole string. Nothing else in key = AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP matches, so the output is key = [REDACTED:aws-access-key-id].

extra_patterns is ("bad", "(unclosed"), which does not compile, and extra_excluded_globs is empty. The test says it must not panic and asserts contains [REDACTED:aws-access-key-id]. It does not assert_eq the whole string. The invalid regex is skipped and the baseline output is key = [REDACTED:aws-access-key-id].
assert!(is_excluded_path(".env", &cfg())). The file name matches the built-in glob .env. cfg() is RedactionConfig::default(): both extra lists empty.
assert!(is_excluded_path("project/.env.local", &cfg())). The file name .env.local matches the built-in glob .env.*. The test asserts the bool, nothing else.
assert!(is_excluded_path("secrets/id_rsa", &cfg())). The file name id_rsa matches the built-in glob id_rsa.
assert!(is_excluded_path("certs/server.pem", &cfg())). The file name server.pem matches the built-in glob *.pem.
assert!(!is_excluded_path("src/main.rs", &cfg())). No built-in glob matches main.rs or src/main.rs.
assert!(!is_excluded_path("ekos.toml", &cfg())). No built-in glob matches ekos.toml.

extra_excluded_globs is ["secrets/*.yaml"] and extra_patterns is empty. assert!(is_excluded_path("secrets/prod.yaml", &config)). The glob matches the relative path, not the bare file name prod.yaml. The test asserts the bool.
Same config as #yaml. assert!(is_excluded_path(".env", &config)). The comment says the baseline still applies alongside the extra glob. .env matches the built-in glob, not secrets/*.yaml.

redact_json of the json! value. The test does not assert the whole document. It asserts excerpt contains [REDACTED:aws-access-key-id], symbols[1] contains that same label, nested.inner contains it, and count == 3. It does not assert symbols[0] (fn main, unchanged), the "key = " or "token: " prefixes, or key order. serde_json's Map is a BTreeMap, so a serialized value would order keys count, excerpt, nested, symbols; the test never serializes, and this object is in the order the literal is written. Each string is redacted on its own. count is a number and is left alone.
